summary: Learn imagery selection, land-cover classification and accuracy assessment. Build defensible monitoring evidence. Explore the course and curriculum.
lede: Satellite-based land-use monitoring uses imagery to map land cover and check whether mapped classes are supported by reference data. For GIS and remote-sensing analysts, the training covers selecting Sentinel imagery, preparing classification inputs, and interpreting spectral features. Participants also plan reference sampling, interpret confusion matrices, and communicate map accuracy and uncertainty for land-use or infrastructure monitoring.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use spatial data to monitor land use, environmental conditions, agricultural programmes, or infrastructure assets. It suits people with existing GIS or data capabilities who need a more defensible image-to-evidence workflow. This course is designed for: GIS analysts preparing land-use maps from satellite imagery. Remote-sensing analysts selecting imagery and interpreting spectral features. Conservation monitoring specialists tracking habitat and land-cover change. Land-management officers validating mapped boundaries and land-use classes. Agricultural programme specialists monitoring crop and rural land conditions. Infrastructure planners checking corridors, sites, and surrounding land-use change. Geospatial data quality specialists designing reference samples and accuracy checks. Environmental monitoring officers preparing validated spatial evidence for reporting. Earth observation team leads reviewing classification methods and map limitations. Programme monitoring and evaluation specialists using geospatial indicators in results reporting.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with GIS concepts, spatial data, and map use is expected. Prior remote-sensing classification experience is helpful but not required. No programming is required for the stated exercises.
